fields.Front: Define the participation constraint, and define total and partial participation with the case-study example of each.
fields.Back:
Participation specifies whether the existence of an entity depends on it being related to another entity via the relationship - it is the MINIMUM number of relationship instances.
Total (mandatory): EVERY entity must participate - every employee must WORK FOR a department. Drawn as a DOUBLE line.
Partial (optional): some but not necessarily all participate - some employees manage a department. Drawn as a SINGLE line.

fields.Front: Explain (min, max) notation and what each number tells you.
fields.Back:
Beside each entity's line write (min, max) with 0 <= min <= max and max >= 1: each entity of that type participates in at least min and at most max relationship instances.
MIN always tells you the PARTICIPATION: 0 means partial, 1 or more means total (and the line must be double).
MAX tells you the CARDINALITY: 1 means a 'one' side, M or N a 'many' side.

fields.Front: What mistake did the instructor catch on her own (min, max) slide, and what should you expect on the exam?
fields.Back: An entity labelled (1, M) had been drawn with a SINGLE line; because the minimum is greater than zero it should have been a DOUBLE line (total participation). 'If the first number is one or greater, this is total participation.' Expect a question that asks you to spot exactly that inconsistency.

fields.Front: Give the (min, max) pairs and reasoning for Person BOOKS Hotel Room, Artist PAINTS Painting and Woman GIVES BIRTH TO Child.
fields.Back:
Person (1,N) BOOKS Hotel Room (0,M), an M:N relationship: 'why would we save information on this person if they haven't started booking rooms?' but a new hotel may have rooms sitting empty.
Artist (0,M) PAINTS Painting (1,1): 'paintings don't just come out of thin air', but some artists have not painted anything yet.
Woman (0,M) GIVES BIRTH TO Child (1,1): not every woman gives birth; every child was born to someone.

fields.Front: APPLICATION: read BRANCH (5, N) --- Is allocated --- (0,1) EMPLOYEE in layers.
fields.Back:
Cardinality: a branch is allocated many employees; an employee works at one branch (1:N).
Participation: the double line at BRANCH says every branch has at least one employee; the single line at EMPLOYEE says not every employee works at a branch.
(0,1) at EMPLOYEE: an employee is allocated to zero or one branch.
(5,N) at BRANCH: every branch has AT LEAST FIVE employees and at most N - a '5-to-many' relationship, which double lines alone cannot express.

fields.Front: How does the instructor reason about the participation of Student TAKES Course and Artist PAINTS Picture?
fields.Back:
Student: total - 'at a university we're not going to store information about people who don't take courses'. Course: possibly partial - 'maybe we don't offer it if nobody's taking it'.
Picture: total - otherwise how did it come into existence? Artist: 'a bit iffy' - the word implies they have painted, but we might store someone who has not painted yet.

fields.Front: Case study: give the participation she assigned to HAS (dependents), WORKS ON and CONTROLS, with her reasoning.
fields.Back:
HAS: EMPLOYEE partial (0,N) - not every employee has a dependent; DEPENDENT total (1,1) - 'we wouldn't keep information about a dependent unless they had a parent who worked at the company'.
WORKS ON: both total (1,N) - every employee should be working on something and 'every project has to have somebody working on it'. She expects you to figure this one out unprompted.
CONTROLS: DEPARTMENT partial (0,N) - not stated; PROJECT total (1,1) - every project is controlled by a department.

fields.Front: Case study: give the participation of WORKS FOR, MANAGES and SUPERVISES, with her reasoning.
fields.Back:
WORKS FOR: EMPLOYEE total (1,1) and DEPARTMENT total (1,N) - every employee works for a department and every department has employees.
MANAGES: EMPLOYEE partial (0,1) - only one person per department is picked; DEPARTMENT total (1,1) - every department must have a manager.
SUPERVISES: both partial - not every employee supervises, and 'the very top boss, the president, probably doesn't have a supervisor'.

fields.Front: APPLICATION: Man FATHERS Child. Give the cardinality, the participation of each side, and the (min, max) pairs.
fields.Back: Cardinality 1:N (a man could father many children; a child has one father). Child: TOTAL - every child has somebody who fathered them, so a double line, (1,1). Man: PARTIAL - not all men are fathers, so a single line, (0,N).

fields.Text: The key word for participation is {{c1::EVERY}}: if every single instance must participate it is {{c1::total}} participation (a {{c1::double line}}); anything less is partial (a single line).

Cardinality ratio gives the {{c1::maximum}} number of instances an entity participates in (1, M or N) and is found with the word '{{c1::could}}'; participation gives the {{c1::minimum}} (total = at least 1, partial = may be 0) and is found with the word 'every'.

In (min, max) notation the {{c1::min}} gives the participation and the {{c1::max}} gives the cardinality; a min of {{c1::0}} means partial; the max beside an entity always matches the Chen letter at the opposite end of the line.

Instructor's promise: 'On an exam, if I ask you a question like this, I will always give you {{c1::enough information}}' to decide total versus partial; in the videos she sometimes relies on {{c1::common sense}} instead.

Case study participation: WORKS FOR {{c1::total on both sides}}; MANAGES - EMPLOYEE {{c1::partial (0,1)}}, DEPARTMENT {{c1::total (1,1)}}; HAS - EMPLOYEE partial, DEPENDENT total; SUPERVISES partial on both sides (the president has no supervisor).

Textbook (Elmasri §3.4.3): total participation is also called {{c1::existence dependency}}; the participation constraint is also called the {{c1::minimum cardinality}} constraint; and cardinality ratio plus participation taken together are the {{c1::structural constraints}} of a relationship type.
